Experience is the master. Chapters of the journal, finished by doing alchemy
book.servus_alchemy.journal.name: Paracelsus' Journal
book.servus_alchemy.journal.opus.basel_s: [storyteller] Basel made me town physician and the professors hated me for it. I lectured in German, not in their Latin, and I gave their great book to the fire. Let them howl!
Then out, at night, like a thief. And Salzburg at the end. The end? Who is writing this?
Red. The Work ends in red. Obsidian that weeps, from beyond the burning gate, more than any broken portal gives. The fire wants a crown. Four pillars. Two stones high. I counted them twice.
Stand two Crying Obsidian on each corner of the yellow ring and the Athanor burns red: Rubedo.
Here the notes break off. The pages after this one are still blank.
book.servus_alchemy.journal.opus.name: The Great Work
book.servus_alchemy.journal.opus.old_gno: One of them followed me out of Schwaz. A grey beard down to his boots, a red cap, a temper like a cracked lamp. He knew more of the mountain than every assayer in Tyrol.

When I left for the road he stayed below, deep in the dark rock, and I never found him again.

If you hear knocking deep in the deepslate, follow it.
In Schwaz the old hewers would stop and listen. A knocking in the rock, where no man worked: the Bergmaennlein, the little miners. Knock before a rich vein, knock before the roof comes down.
The wise ones left them bread and a pinch of salt, and laughed at nobody.
Miners in far lands, I am told, call them Knockers and leave them the crust of their pasty. Every mine has its little people, and every honest miner knows it.
This is not part of the Great Work. It is an old man's errand.
Mine deep, below the stone, where the deepslate is. If he hears this journal he will knock. Follow the knocking; where dust trickles from one block, look for the things he leaves behind.
Then drink the Elixir of Sight, and hold this journal up to him.
book.servus_alchemy.journal.opus.preface: These are the notes of Theophrastus von Hohenheim, who called himself Paracelsus.
I learned from the furnace, the mine and the sickbed, not from old books. Experience is the master. Follow these pages by doing the work, and each chapter of my life will open to you.
In the silver mines of Schwaz in Tyrol I worked among the miners and saw the sickness the mountain gives them.
The old miners say that metals grow in the rock like plants, and that small spirits of the earth live in the galleries. If the mountain grows its ores, perhaps it can be asked to.
Salt is the body of all things. Press nine Salt Crystals into a block, eight such blocks into a ring around your Athanor, and its flame turns white: Albedo.
The spirits of the earth live in the rock as we live in air, and common eyes do not see them. On a white Athanor, Quicksilver and the three principles give the Elixir of Sight. But mind the dose:
the dose makes the poison, and now and then the elixir bites back.
The miners of Schwaz say the metals grow in the mountain like roots, tended by gnomes. Burn cracked stone bricks with Salt and Mercury on a white Athanor into a Gnome Hollow.

To common eyes it is stone. Drink the elixir and offer it a Salt Crystal: a gnome takes it and moves in. Raw ore will not take root.

The seed of a metal does, and the white Athanor makes the seeds of iron and copper.
Give one to the gnome, pour Salt and Mercury in until the vein is ripe, and he digs that ore for you, for as long as the Hollow stands.
book.servus_alchemy.journal.opus.villach: Every alchemist needs a furnace that never goes out. Build an Athanor of bricks, a blast furnace and a cauldron.

Lay an item on it and feed it principles by bucket or pipe; it burns them into something new.

The stones you set around it decide how far its fire reaches. Alone it burns black, the fire of Nigredo.
My father was a physician in Villach, in Carinthia, a country of mines and smelters. There I first watched ore turn into metal in the fire.

Every body is made of three: Salt, which gives it form, Sulfur, which burns, and Mercury, the spirit that flies off. Burn a thing in the Calciner and the three part from each other.

Join them again in the Coagulator.
Finishing Villach opens the next chapter of the journal: Schwaz, and the mines.
book.servus_alchemy.journal.opus.wanderi: [storyteller] Roads. Years of roads, I stopped counting, the counting stopped me. Every town its own quack, every university the same dead Latin.
I learned more from barbers, hangmen and the old women who sell herbs than from all the doctors and their Galen. Write that down. I am writing it down!
The gnomes of Schwaz laughed at my iron. Iron is for nails, they said. Feed us better and we dig the sun out of the rock. The sun! Yellow fire, yellow stone. Or bile. The same thing, the same thing.
Set a Principle Vat beside each tank of the white Athanor and offer it an Amethyst Block: citrine grows in the vats and the Athanor burns yellow: Citrinitas.
Its fire makes nobler seeds, of gold and of redstone, and a ripe vein of gold proves them.
Finishing the Wandering years opens the next chapter of the journal: Basel and Salzburg, and the red fire.
book.servus_alchemy.journal.tooltip: Notes of Theophrastus von Hohenheim. Experience is the master.
book.servus_alchemy.journal.workshop.ame: Four shards of the violet crystal that grows in the hollow stones of the deep make a block. Heated in the white fire, amethyst turns into yellow citrine, the stone Citrinitas is named after.
Beside each tank, on its outer side three blocks from the Athanor, set an empty Principle Vat on the hearth level. Then use an Amethyst Block on the white Athanor:
it rises, bursts into three streams of light, and a cluster of citrine grows out of each vat. The flame turns yellow.
Break a grown vat and the citrine falls to shards; the fire is white again until the ritual is cast anew.
Three empty Principle Vats beside the tanks of the white Athanor; then offer it an Amethyst Block. Press Visualize, then click the ground.
The yellow fire makes nobler seeds: the Seed of Gold from Raw Gold, the Seed of Redstone from Redstone Dust and the Seed of Quartz from Nether Quartz.

Only the red fire makes the Seed of Diamond from Diamond and the Seed of Emerald from Emerald.

Noble veins drink more Salt and Mercury, the diamond Sulfur as well, and the gnomes dig them slower.
book.servus_alchemy.journal.workshop.ath: Set it on a hearth of Bricks and Brick Slabs with a Brick Stair in front, stand three Fluid Tanks three high to its left, behind it and to its right, lay a Copper Duct from the Athanor to each tank, and use this journal on it. Press Visualize, then click the ground.
The Athanor on its Hearth
The furnace that never goes out
Use an item on it to lay it on top. It burns what its tanks hold, and the work lies on top when it is done: take it with an empty hand, or sneak to take the item back. Hoppers and pipes may do both.
Its Fire
Alone its flame is black: Nigredo. A ring of Salt Crystal Blocks under its hearth turns the flame white: Albedo.

An Amethyst Block offered to it grows citrine in Principle Vats beside its tanks and turns it yellow: Citrinitas. Pillars of Crying Obsidian beside the back tank and behind the side tanks turn it red:
Rubedo. Some works need a higher fire.
The Athanor burns only on a hearth of 3 by 3 right below it: Bricks under it and in front of it, a bottom Brick Slab on each of the other seven cells, and a Brick Stair in front as the step.
Its Hearth
Three Fluid Tanks stand two blocks out, each three high from the hearth up, and a Copper Duct beside the Athanor leads to each. When all is laid, use this journal on the Athanor:
it rises into a brick tower with a fire door and the ducts become pipes into its tanks. Take a brick, a slab, a tank or a duct away and its fire goes out.
Lay an item on it, feed it principles, and it burns them into something new.
The Athanor
The Athanor
Stone Bricks, a cauldron and a blast furnace.
The Athanor keeps no principles of its own. It drinks them from its three Fluid Tanks, two blocks out to its left, behind it and to its right, so they never touch and never run together.
Its Tanks
Any tank may hold any principle. Lead pipes to them or pour buckets in. Each tank of three is one big tank.

- Salt Crystal Block from Salt Crystal: 1000 Salt
- Blaze Powder from Gunpowder: 200 Sulfur
- Bottle o' Enchanting from Glass Bottle: 50 Salt, 100 Mercury (Albedo)
Its Works

- Elixir of Sight from Quicksilver: 100 Salt, 100 Sulfur, 250 Mercury (Albedo)
- Gnome Hollow from Cracked Stone Bricks: 500 Salt, 250 Mercury (Albedo)
- Principle Dropper from Principle Vat: 250 Salt, 250 Sulfur, 250 Mercury (Citrinitas)
- Ignis Perpetuus from Sal Ammoniac: 500 Sulfur (Citrinitas)

- Sealed Flask from Crying Obsidian: 250 Salt, 500 Mercury (Rubedo)
- Prelum Screw from Dragon's Breath: 500 Sulfur, 500 Mercury (Rubedo)
- Seed of Coal from Coal: 150 Salt, 150 Sulfur (Albedo)
- Seed of Iron from Raw Iron: 250 Salt, 100 Mercury (Albedo)

- Seed of Copper from Raw Copper: 250 Salt, 100 Mercury (Albedo)
- Seed of Gold from Raw Gold: 250 Salt, 250 Sulfur, 250 Mercury (Citrinitas)
- Seed of Redstone from Redstone Dust: 250 Sulfur, 250 Mercury (Citrinitas)
- Seed of Quartz from Nether Quartz: 250 Salt, 250 Mercury (Citrinitas)

- Seed of Diamond from Diamond: 500 Salt, 500 Sulfur, 500 Mercury (Rubedo)
- Seed of Emerald from Emerald: 500 Salt, 500 Sulfur, 500 Mercury (Rubedo)
book.servus_alchemy.journal.workshop.cal: A wall one block deep with a tank on each side. Press Visualize, then click the ground where it shall stand.
The Calciner

- Cobblestone: 100 Salt, 10 Mercury
- Stone: 100 Salt, 10 Mercury
- Dirt: 50 Salt, 20 Sulfur, 20 Mercury
- Sand: 80 Salt, 10 Mercury
- Gravel: 80 Salt, 10 Mercury
What Burns

- Logs: 20 Salt, 100 Sulfur, 10 Mercury
- Planks: 5 Salt, 25 Sulfur
- Leaves: 40 Sulfur, 20 Mercury
- Saplings: 40 Sulfur, 20 Mercury
- Crops: 10 Salt, 30 Sulfur, 30 Mercury
- Seeds: 10 Salt, 30 Sulfur, 30 Mercury

- Coal: 200 Sulfur
- Raw ore: 150 Salt, 50 Mercury
- Redstone: 100 Mercury
- Bones: 100 Salt
Burn matter into its principles
Each principle leaves where it belongs. Salt stays behind as ash in the Ash Pan.
Taking Them Out
Mercury cools in the Receiver, drips from its tap into the basin and runs down into the right tank, and Sulfur rises into the Hood and runs down the duct into the left tank.
Take them from the tanks with a bucket, or with a pipe whose side at the tank you set to pull in with the carrot: a tank on a plain side only ever fills.
The Salt stays in the Ash Pan as Ash, one Ash for every 100 Salt. Take it with an empty hand, or put a hopper under the Ash Pan, and wash it in the Purifier.
The Ash Pan holds a stack of 64 Ash; when it is full, the Calciner waits.
Hand the matter to the mouth, or let a hopper or a pipe feed it. Coal and other fuel go into the Firebox below; one coal burns for several items.
Firing It

Sneak with an empty hand at the mouth to take the matter back.

When a tank or the Ash Pan is full, the Calciner waits.
Set Ignis Perpetuus into the Firebox and it burns forever without fuel and calcines faster. Sneak with an empty hand at the Firebox to take it back.
My furnace for the first work. It burns a thing until only its three principles are left.
The Calciner
The Calciner
Three parts stack in the middle: the Ash Pan at the bottom between Deepslate Tiles, the Firebox above it between two Fluid Tanks, and the Calciner, the mouth, between Stone Bricks.
The Parts
On top of the mouth sits the Alembic, the copper still, and the Sulfur Hood crowns it.
The Receiver, a copper condenser, stands right of the still over a stone basin, and the still's beak leads into it. The Copper Duct leads from the Hood down into the left Stone Bricks.
The mouth with its cauldron, and the Firebox.
The Copper Duct, three at once.
The Ash Pan and the Alembic.
The Receiver and the Sulfur Hood.
When every block stands, use this journal on the Calciner. The stones join and the furnace becomes one thing. If something is missing, the journal tells you what and where.
Waking It
Break any block and the furnace falls apart into its stones and parts again.
book.servus_alchemy.journal.workshop.coa: Three Principle Vats over a casting table between Stone Bricks. Press Visualize, then click the ground.
Set the Coagulator between two Stone Bricks and put a Principle Vat on each of the three. The left Vat takes Sulfur, the middle one Salt and the right one Mercury, the same sides as at the Calciner.
Use this journal on the Coagulator to bring the build together; break any block and it falls apart.
Join the principles into a body
Open the Coagulator with an empty hand, press the select button and choose what to make. Then bring the principles: by pipe or bucket into their Vats, or on a gauge in the GUI.
A hopper or pipe feeds the ingredient into the table and takes the products from it.
It joins the principles again into a body. It needs no fire, only time to cool.

- Salt Crystal: 250 Salt
- Sulfur: 250 Sulfur
- Quicksilver: 250 Mercury
- Clay Ball: 100 Salt, 50 Mercury
- Flint: 150 Salt

- Gunpowder: 50 Salt, 150 Sulfur
- Redstone: 50 Salt, 150 Mercury
- Glowstone Dust: 100 Sulfur, 100 Mercury
- Bone Meal: 60 Salt, 20 Sulfur
- Slimeball: 50 Sulfur, 150 Mercury
The casting table, and a Principle Vat; you need three.
book.servus_alchemy.journal.workshop.cry: Obsidian that weeps. A ruined portal holds a little, the Piglins of the Nether trade it for gold, and the chests of their bastions keep more.
Stand four pillars of two Crying Obsidian on the white ring, from the hearth level up: one on each side of the tank behind the Athanor and one behind each side tank, eight blocks in all.
Then the flame turns red: Rubedo.
Four pillars of Crying Obsidian beside the back tank and behind the side tanks. Press Visualize, then click the ground.
book.servus_alchemy.journal.workshop.eli: Lay Quicksilver on a white Athanor and feed it 100 Salt, 100 Sulfur, 250 Mercury.
Albedo: see what lives in the rock
The dose makes the poison. Now and then a drink sickens you: poison and a spinning head for a few breaths, though the sight comes all the same.
Drink again while the sight still lasts and the risk grows.
Drink it and for a few minutes you see the spirits of the earth and what they tend.
book.servus_alchemy.journal.workshop.gno: Albedo: a vein that grows
Gnomes have a sweet tooth. Under the sight, hand a working gnome a cookie, bread or berries and it digs twice as fast for a while. It needs no gifts to work; it only works slower without them.
Gifts
Anything else it will not touch.
Drink the Elixir of Sight first. To common eyes the Hollow is only stone, and it answers no one who cannot see.
Calling the Gnome
Under the sight, use a Salt Crystal on the empty Hollow. A gnome takes it and moves in. He waits for a seed to plant.
Pour Salt and Mercury in by bucket. No pipe reaches it. Step by step the vein ripens while the gnome tends it, and once ripe he digs its ore for you, as long as the Hollow stands.
Growing a Vein
Give him the seed of another metal and he digs the old vein out and plants the new one. The old vein is lost; what he dug stays in his store.
A home for a gnome. To common eyes it is only stone.
Gnome Hollow
Lay Cracked Stone Bricks on a white Athanor and feed it 500 Salt, 250 Mercury.
Making It
Break the Hollow under the sight and you get an empty Hollow back, with the ore from its store. The vein, its principles and its gnome are lost.
Moving It
Break it without the sight and it is only stone.
Gnome Hollow
Raw ore does not take root; the gnome wants the seed of a metal. The Athanor makes them:
Seeds of Metals

the Seed of Coal from Coal, the Seed of Iron from Raw Iron and the Seed of Copper from Raw Copper on a white Athanor. Nobler seeds need a hotter fire.

Give the seed to the Hollow and the gnome plants it.
The gnome keeps what it digs in a small store inside the Hollow and stops when the store is full. Use an empty hand on the Hollow, under the sight, to take the ore out.
The Gnome's Store
After a new seed, take the old ore out before he digs the new one.
book.servus_alchemy.journal.workshop.kno: Signs of what the eye cannot see

What lives in the elements hides from common eyes, but not from common ears. First you hear it: a knocking in the rock, and it comes from somewhere, so follow it. Closer, dust trickles from one block.

Closest of all, you find what they leave behind: a tiny pickaxe, a scrap of red felt, a little bowl of salt.

Then drink the Elixir of Sight, and look.
A gnome at work in a Gnome Hollow knocks softly now and then. A salamander in the lava of the Nether shows as a flame that dances a little too long.

The homunculus in its Vas stirs the liquid by itself.

And deep in the deepslate, if you have walked with me to Schwaz, someone older may knock for you.
book.servus_alchemy.journal.workshop.pip: A Fluid Pipe moves principles between blocks. Every pipe arm that touches a block has a channel colour, and only arms of the same channel trade.
Set the channel with the carrot on the arm that touches the block.
A machine side has two settings. The Items tab says what items do there. The Fluids tab says which principle goes in or out: Off, All, or one principle.

The carrot works on one of them; use it on the air to switch between Items and Fluids.

The Calciner has no sides to set: each principle leaves through its own part.
book.servus_alchemy.journal.workshop.pre: Rubedo: the press at the end of the Work
The screw over a Heavy Weighted Pressure Plate between two Stripped Dark Oak Logs, on Polished Deepslate.
Lay Dragon's Breath on a red Athanor and feed it 500 Sulfur, 500 Mercury. One bottle from the End, once: the screw does not wear out.
[storyteller] The dead head! Caput Mortuum, the worthless earth that stays when the Salt is gone. For years I swept it out of the vat and they laughed.

Press it, I say, press it hard enough and long enough and the dead head gives up the black metal of the burning world. The dragon's breath makes the screw. I have seen the dragon. Or I dreamt it.

The screw is real.
Lay 16 Caput Mortuum in the left slot. The press needs no fire and no principles; it turns its bar, lowers its plate and after 30 seconds gives one Netherite Scrap.
Smith four scraps with four Gold Ingots into a Netherite Ingot.
Hoppers and Item Pipes feed it from any side but the front, and it pushes its scrap into a chest beside it. On a data line it presses what a Crafting CPU orders.
book.servus_alchemy.journal.workshop.pri: The drops only ripen the vein. Binding the gnome with a Salt Crystal and taking its ore out remain your work, under the sight.
Still by Hand
Citrinitas: the Hollow fed by drops
A vat taught to weep. It lets the principles fall drop by drop, so no pipe need ever touch the Hollow.
Principle Dropper
Lay Principle Vat on a yellow Athanor and feed it 250 Salt, 250 Sulfur, 250 Mercury.
Making It
Principle Dropper
Set the Dropper right on top of a Gnome Hollow and lead Salt, Sulfur and Mercury into it with a Fluid Pipe, or pour buckets in. Each principle has its own small tank.
Using It
While the vein below is seeded and not yet ripe, the Dropper lets fall what the vein drinks, a few drops at a time, and the vein ripens without your buckets.
A ripe vein, an empty Hollow or plain stone gets nothing; the Dropper keeps its principles and pours them into nothing else.
Salt, Sulfur and Mercury
A Fluid Tank holds one principle at a time, so give each principle its own tank.
Keeping Them
Poured on the ground they spread like water but never make a new source. What you do not need, pour into a Sink.
The Three Principles
Every body is made of three. Salt gives it form, Sulfur makes it burn, and Mercury is the spirit that flies off. In the fire the Salt stays behind as Ash; the Purifier washes it into liquid Salt.
The Three
In this work they are liquids. They flow through Fluid Pipes, rest in Fluid Tanks and fill buckets.
book.servus_alchemy.journal.workshop.pur: The Vat on a log of any wood, the Basin on one side of the log and the Crock on the other, either way round. Press Visualize, then click the ground.
Wash the Salt out of the Ash
Use this journal on the Vat to bring the build together. Give the Vat Ash by hand, by hopper or by pipe, and water by bucket or by pipe from a pump.

Four Ash at a time give up their Salt, and it runs into the Basin.

Take the Salt from the Basin with an empty bucket, or pipe it away. Take the Caput Mortuum from the Crock with an empty hand, or set a hopper under it.
Sneak with an empty hand on the Vat to take the Ash back. Keep the Caput Mortuum: nothing in the Great Work is worthless forever.

A leaching vat on a log. Water washes the Salt out of the Ash and runs down into the catch basin as the Salt the Coagulator needs; what stays behind is Caput Mortuum, the dead head, and it falls into the residue crock.
The Leaching Vat and the Catch Basin.
- 4 Ash and 400 mB water: 400 Salt and 1 Caput Mortuum
book.servus_alchemy.journal.workshop.rec: A chest with a fire in its belly. What my little helper gathers falls into it, and its fire keeps him warm, as every homunculus must be kept warm.
Rubedo: the warm chest below the glass
Ignis Perpetuus between Deepslate Bricks, a Chest above it and a hearth of Bricks below.
The upper row holds three gifts for the gnomes on the left and the Elixir of Sight on the right. Below lie twenty-seven slots for the yield; you may only take from them.
Hoppers and Item Pipes take the yield out on every side but the front and bring gifts and Elixir in. Pipe nothing else into it: whatever is no Elixir lands among the gifts.
On a data line a Crafting CPU orders ore from it as from any machine.
book.servus_alchemy.journal.workshop.sal: Citrinitas: the fire that eats gold
Set Ignis Perpetuus into the Firebox of a Calciner and it fires the Calciner forever, without coal, and makes it calcine faster. Sneak with an empty hand at the Firebox to take it back.
The Eternal Flame
Hold out a Gold Ingot to a salamander you can see. It eats every ingot, and now and then it takes a liking to you: hearts, and it is yours. A befriended salamander shows itself to everyone.
Gold for a Friend
It follows you, even through the lava, and finds you when you go too far. Click it with an empty hand to make it sit or stand. It likes to lie in a lit campfire.
Lay Sal Ammoniac on a yellow Athanor and feed it 500 Sulfur. The flame that never goes out. It does not feed a furnace; it fires a Calciner and is built into greater works.
Ignis Perpetuus
The Salamander
Feed your salamander a Gold Ingot and wait a minute. It gives back one lump of Sal Ammoniac. One ingot at a time; it will not take the next before it is done.
Sal Ammoniac
The salamanders, lizards of glowing coal, live in the Nether's crimson forests, near the crimson trees and the Nether Wart. Fewer live among the warped trees; now and then one swims on lava.
Among the Crimson Stems
Without the sight you see only a flame that dances a little too long. Drink the Elixir of Sight and you see them. Fire and lava do them no harm, and they harm nobody.
Citrinitas: the furnace that needs no coal
A furnace with the eternal flame shut inside. It has eaten its last lump of coal.
The Salamander Forge
The Salamander Forge
Ignis Perpetuus over a Furnace, walled in Deepslate Bricks.
It smelts what a furnace smelts, as fast as a furnace, and never asks for fuel. Its fire burns day and night and lights the room around it.
Using It
Lay the ore in the top slot and take the metal from the right. Hoppers and Item Pipes feed it from any side but the front, and it pushes its work into a chest beside it.
On a data line it smelts what a Crafting CPU orders.
A Salt Crystal grown whole on the Athanor. Sixteen of them in a ring under its hearth make its flame white.
Salt Crystal Block
Albedo: the white ring
No hand can press Salt into a block. Lay a Salt Crystal from the Coagulator on the Athanor and give its tanks 1000 Salt: the fire grows the crystal into a block.
Growing It
Salt Crystal Block
Sixteen Salt Crystal Blocks in a 5 by 5 ring one layer under the hearth, so the tanks and the edge of the hearth stand on it. Press Visualize, then click the ground.
The White Ring
book.servus_alchemy.journal.workshop.vas: Lay Crying Obsidian on a red Athanor and feed it 250 Salt, 500 Mercury. Set it on a Receptaculum; it stands nowhere else.
Lay the Elixir of Sight into the Receptaculum's Elixir slot. The homunculus grows while it drinks, two days and two nights, and the Elixir runs out as it grows and as it works.

Without the Elixir it sleeps and waits.

Break the glass and it is gone; a new flask starts a new one from the seed.
They laughed in Basel when I wrote it down. Seal the seed in the glass, keep it warm forty days, feed it the arcanum, and a little man grows in it, wiser than the fool who made it.
They laugh no more. Mine sits in his glass and works for me, my faithful little helper, and he never complains.
Grown, it reaches every Gnome Hollow on the Receptaculum's level, two blocks to every side.

It takes the ore the gnomes dug and lays it into the Receptaculum, and when a gnome tires it brings it a gift from the gift slots.

Only the sight shows him at his work. Do not listen too closely to what he mutters.
gui.servus_alchemy.coagulator.none.toolt: The Coagulator stops and keeps its principles
item.servus_alchemy.ignis_perpetuus.quot: Do not ask what it is. It burns forever, that is all you need to know.
item.servus_alchemy.prelum_screw.quote: Iron that has breathed the dragon's breath does not bend. It turns, and it presses, and it never tires.
item.servus_alchemy.red_felt_scrap.quote: Torn from a little red cap. I have seen such caps before, in Schwaz.
item.servus_alchemy.sal_ammoniac.quote: The salamander gives back what it eats, only better. Do not tell the goldsmiths.
item.servus_alchemy.salt_offering.quote: An offering, left in the dark. The miners did the same for the little ones.
item.servus_alchemy.tiny_pickaxe.quote: Too small for any hand I know. Somebody is digging down there.
jade.servus_alchemy.gnome_hollow.gnome_w: A gnome waits for a seed

message.servus_alchemy.elixir_of_sight.p: The dose makes the poison! Too much, you fool, too much.
message.servus_alchemy.gnome_hollow.boun: A gnome takes your offering and moves into the hollow.
message.servus_alchemy.gnome_hollow.gift: The gnome wrinkles its nose. It does not want this.
No gnome is here to take a gift.
The gnome takes your gift and digs with a will.
message.servus_alchemy.gnome_hollow.no_g: No gnome lives here yet. Offer him a Salt Crystal.
message.servus_alchemy.gnome_hollow.no_v: The gnome waits for a seed to plant.
message.servus_alchemy.gnome_hollow.not_: The gnome turns it over and hands it back. He wants a seed.
message.servus_alchemy.gnome_hollow.refu: The hollow takes none of this.
message.servus_alchemy.gnome_hollow.swap: The gnome digs out the old vein and plants the seed.
message.servus_alchemy.gnome_hollow.unkn: This seed will not take root.
message.servus_alchemy.gnome_hollow.work: A gnome is at work. Nothing to take yet.
message.servus_alchemy.homunculus.secret: [storyteller] The glass breaks. The little one climbs onto the rim and looks at you.
[storyteller] "Thank you. Now listen, and I will tell you what he never wrote down."
[storyteller] "I will stay and work for you. Not because I must. Because you asked."
message.servus_alchemy.homunculus.whispe: [storyteller] Is there a star? I saw one, once, through the glass.
[storyteller] He says the chain is for my own good.
[storyteller] A star would burn the chain. A star would burn the glass.
[storyteller] Keep the fire warm. Please keep the fire warm.
message.servus_alchemy.old_gnome.greetin: [storyteller] "Theophrastus? No... but that is his book. Sit, sit. I have waited a long time."
message.servus_alchemy.old_gnome.trace: They are near. Drink, and look.
message.servus_alchemy.purifier.at.on_th: on the other side of the log
message.servus_alchemy.purifier.missing: The Purifier is not complete: %s needed %s. The Purifier page of Paracelsus' Journal shows the build.
